concepts.title: Mahajanapadas and the Rise of Magadha
concepts.definition: Between about the sixth and fourth centuries BCE, sixteen mahajanapadas competed; Magadha rose to dominance through its iron-rich hills, elephants, the fertile Ganga valley and powerful rulers like Bimbisara and Ajatasattu who built fortifications and absorbed neighbours.
concepts.key_idea: Resources plus ruthless statecraft, not legitimacy alone, won the early state competition.
concepts.textbook_ref: lehs102.txt mahajanapadas list and Magadha's most powerful sections

solution_steps.explain: sixteen mahajanapadas are named in early texts
iron ore, elephants and riverine fertility underpinned its armies
fortified capitals and annexations turned Magadha into the empire's base

concepts.title: The Mauryan Empire and Asoka's Dhamma
concepts.definition: The Mauryan empire under Chandragupta and Asoka organised administration through provincial capitals, a treasury and officials; Asoka's inscriptions in Prakrit across the subcontinent proclaimed dhamma - respect for elders, generosity to friends, tolerance of sects - and appointed dhamma mahamattas to spread it.
concepts.key_idea: Asoka ruled by inscription as much as by army: rock and pillar edicts carried a moral vocabulary across regions and centuries.

solution_steps.explain: a code of social ethics rather than a single religion

dhamma mahamattas institutionalised welfare and teaching

concepts.title: Coins, Kings and Cities
concepts.definition: From the sixth century BCE punch-marked coins of silver and copper circulated through towns with guilds (shrenis) of artisans and merchants; by the first millennium CE, larger states, temple building and elite claims of divine kingship reshaped political imagination while Sanskrit rose as a court language.
concepts.key_idea: Money, towns and shrenis grew together, and coins stamped with rulers - like the Gupta gold dinars - advertised kingship itself.

solution_steps.explain: punch-marked silver circulated in the earliest towns

concepts.title: Land Grants and Agrarian Expansion
concepts.definition: From the early centuries CE kings recorded land grants to brahmanas on copper plates and stone, claiming tax-free status for recipients; these grants document agrarian expansion into forests and new regions while revealing conflicts over land rights.
concepts.key_idea: Grants opened new lands to cultivation and anchored brahmana settlements, spreading both agriculture and Sanskritic norms.

concepts.title: The Long Early Historic Span
concepts.definition: The chapter's early historic span runs from about 600 BCE to 600 CE; subtracting the beginning from the end gives the length of this millennium-and-a-half of state formation, trade and change.
concepts.key_idea: Adding the BCE starting year to the CE ending year yields the total span, since BCE years count backwards.
